p: Lakeside is a bit of a magnet for south Essex and beyond, and for good reason. It's a huge shopping and leisure area in West Thurrock, built around a lake, with restaurants and a cinema to keep you busy long after the shops close. A games bar here is a natural way to turn a shopping trip into a proper evening out.

Getting here is mostly about the roads. Lakeside sits close to junction 30 and 31 of the M25 and just off the A13, and there are big car parks around the centre. If you're coming by train, Chafford Hundred station is right by the shopping centre and has services to London Fenchurch Street. Buses run from Grays and the surrounding towns too.

Because Lakeside draws so many people, weekends can be busy, especially around Christmas and school holidays. If you're planning a group outing, try to book early and arrive in good time, as finding a parking space close to your entrance can take a while on a busy Saturday. Weeknights are usually a calmer bet if your group can manage it.

If you've got time to spare, Grays itself sits on the Thames, with a small riverside beach and park that gives you a different view of the busy river. Further along, Tilbury Fort is a well-preserved star-shaped fort run by English Heritage, with a long history guarding the approach to London. And the Queen Elizabeth II Bridge, part of the Dartford Crossing, is an impressive sight from the Essex side.
